recommendation: Keep this source change. It restores the original applied clarification without altering later Location-header or ETag semantics, and no additional work-group review appears necessary.
issue_request: FHIR-13498 was Published/Persuasive and asked the FHIR-core HTTP page to explicitly state that PUTting a resource to a location where a resource previously lived, after deletion, uses 201 Created, while describing the case as bringing the resource back to life and preserving history.
initial_application: The original application was git commit 7b16fff931930a9054083771bbbad8bdd1b5cf06, imported from svn revision 12840, which added a brought-back-to-life/re-created qualifier to the update response sentence requiring 201 Created for created resources.
additional_context: The current source retained the delete-section note that deleted resources may be brought back to life and the version-history explanation, but FHIR-26358 later refactored the same update response paragraph for Location-header requirements and dropped the explicit qualifier. FHIR-25038 later quoted update response wording that retained the brought-back-to-life parenthetical while clarifying ETag optionality.
reconciliation: Changed source/http.html so the update interaction's 201 Created rule explicitly includes creating a current version by bringing a previously deleted resource back to life, and fixed the adjacent delete note's broken update anchor from #href to #update.
source_changes: source/http.html: added a parenthetical to the update 201 Created sentence covering previously deleted resources brought back to life.
source/http.html: corrected the delete-section update cross-reference from #href to #update.

related_jiras.note: Refactored the update response paragraph for Location-header requirements and removed the FHIR-13498 qualifier while making a separate clarification.
Later ETag clarification quoted update response wording with the brought-back-to-life parenthetical, supporting restoration of the qualifier while preserving SHOULD ETag behavior.
